evidence.description: The month is assigned before the throwing serialization and report decoding operation.

candidates.explanation: If serialization or decoding throws, latestMonth has already changed while latestReport retains its previous value. The failed update therefore leaves the publicly readable month and report describing different reporting periods.
candidates.title: Failed decoding leaves partially updated state

evidence.description: A shared instance exposes mutable reporting state.
The asynchronous update method suspends for a network request without actor isolation or synchronization.
The update writes both shared properties without synchronization.

candidates.explanation: The shared instance has no actor isolation or other synchronization around its mutable properties. Concurrent callers can race when reading and writing this state, and overlapping requests can overwrite a newer result with an older one that finishes later.
candidates.title: Unsynchronized shared mutable state

evidence.description: The formatter for machine-readable month keys specifies a format and time zone but leaves its locale and calendar implicit.

candidates.explanation: DateFormatter uses user-dependent defaults for the unspecified locale and calendar. Consequently, fixed year-month keys can be interpreted using a non-Gregorian calendar or formatted differently across user settings, changing which dates are selected or which dictionary key is looked up.
candidates.title: Machine-readable dates depend on user settings

evidence.description: Original dictionary keys are converted to dates and discarded.
The selected date is reformatted with yyyy-M and that generated string is used for the dictionary lookup.

candidates.explanation: Parsing and formatting a date does not preserve the original key spelling. For example, a zero-padded key such as "2023-06" can parse successfully but format back as "2023-6". The subsequent lookup then misses the existing report and substitutes an empty object, causing decoding to fail.
candidates.title: Reconstructed month keys can miss existing reports

evidence.description: The network response is discarded while its body is retained.
The response body is parsed without checking the HTTP status.

candidates.explanation: URLSession does not throw solely because an HTTP response has an error status. Discarding the response means error bodies are treated as report data: they can produce misleading parsing errors or update the report if their structure happens to match the expected payload.
candidates.title: HTTP error status is ignored
